summary: The frozen released HVR validator accepts an empty-source pour because its OR parser discards all source-liquid alternatives. Core implementation impact is demonstrated; historical benchmark effect is unresolved.
scope: Proceedings PDF Sections 2–4 and relevant Appendix B/C/D; static released validator and selected caller/action-admissibility paths; independent regex/Boolean and displayed-table arithmetic only.
limitations: Historical experimental commit correspondence not established.
External OpenReview attachments unavailable in preparation; later revisions not adjudicated.
Other action/effect branches not exhaustively verified.

problems.title: Empty-source pour passes the released core validator
problems.claim: The custom validator checks declared conjunctive/disjunctive atomic preconditions and drives feasibility/correction.
assumptions: Existing normalized Bottle-1 and Cup-1 instances; empty source has valid state metadata.
Source is held and picked up, robot is at empty fillable destination.
No source coffee/wine/water facts; both objects may have ordinary fillable/type facts.
problems.check: Independent regular expression evaluation yields [] for both actual OR strings; Boolean conjunction is false. Static control flow instead returns True and caller does not record failure.
problems.result: Demonstrated false acceptance under the action's own declared preconditions.
problems.counterevidence: Action admissibility is class-based; effect handler with an ordinary empty state prints missing liquid without rejecting. Simulator/goal checking could later fail but does not fix earlier validation.
problems.impact: Core precondition-soundness failure in frozen released validator. No numerical historical benchmark harm claimed.

correction.description: Every OR group must be retained, instantiated and evaluated as any(atom); groups conjoined. Regex-only repair is insufficient.
